legend: Basal palisading of tumour cells along the tumour–brain interface, epithelial whorls, stellate reticulum, and wet keratin.
Tumour extending into adjacent brain tissue, which has reactive changes including piloid gliosis and Rosenthal fibres. Epithelial whorling is commonly present in protrusions.
High-power view of the interface of adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma and brain tissue; Rosenthal fibres are present in the reactive piloid gliosis.

Even though mutations in exon 3 of the CTNNB1 gene, which encodes β-catenin, are clonal and present across the neoplastic epithelium, β-catenin protein only accumulates in the nucleus in subset of cells, such as those that are scattered individually and present in small clusters.

Recurrence 19 years after resection and radiation treatment of an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma that was previously CNS WHO grade 1. Sheets of poorly differentiated cells showing severe cytological atypia, large vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, mitotic activity, and foci of necrosis.

High-power view of malignant craniopharyngioma emerging 19 years after resection and radiation treatment of an adamantinomatous craniopharyngioma that was previously CNS WHO grade 1. Sheets of poorly differentiated cells showing severe cytological atypia, large vesicular nuclei, prominent nucleoli, mitotic activity, and necrosis.
Characteristic very high tumour cell proliferation in malignant craniopharyngioma, as indicated by the Ki-67 index.
A solid and cystic mass with calcification (arrow), first diagnosed 4 years earlier.
A 6-year-old girl presented with severe headache and vomiting. MRI disclosed a large cystic and solid mixed suprasellar tumour with unilateral hydrocephalus. She also showed panhypopituitarism.
A 6-year-old girl presented with severe headache and vomiting. MRI disclosed a large cystic and solid mixed suprasellar tumour with unilateral hydrocephalus. She also showed panhypopituitarism.

The tumour consists of tumour epithelium that can be arranged in cords, lobules, ribbons, nodular whorls, and irregular trabeculae. Basal palisading is prominent in this example. Nodules of anuclear ghost-like squamous cells termed “wet keratin” are scattered throughout the tissue. Stellate reticulum (loose microcystic areas of the tumour) is common through the tumour epithelium interfacing with the wet keratin, whorls, basal palisading perimeter, and more densely arranged areas of tumour epithelium with sheet-like growth. Thin and flattened epithelium from cyst lining can be present in some examples, as can be degenerative changes (fibrosis, calcification) and xanthogranulomatous reaction when cysts rupture. In this example, there is abundant infiltration and adherence of the tumour.
